intended_sample.purpose: Measure a deliberately small but still appropriate Taskledger planning-and-execution run.
intended_sample.interpretation: Do not directly compare its raw totals or per-task average with the financial-tracker server-architecture portfolio. Treat it as a new small-scope family and compare workflow overhead, planning structure, and any defensibly matched task families separately.

git_baseline.note: The status fingerprint and category counts identify the pre-run working-tree state without copying file contents into the benchmark. Recompute and explain any difference before assigning work.

existing_ledger_baseline.interpretation: The next approved specification should be additive to this completed durable history. New-run progress is the delta after this checkpoint, not the lifetime project total.

repository_model_configuration.interpretation: This model change prevents a fair direct token-reduction comparison with the financial-tracker matched cohorts. Keep observed cohorts separate. The run remains useful for small-scope Taskledger overhead and becomes a baseline for later Terra/Luna runs. For the strongest v0.3.0 efficiency proof, restore Sol/high plus Terra/medium before the run begins.

qualification_requirements: The root Taskledger task starts after this checkpoint timestamp.
The injected Taskledger skill and installed CLI are verified as version 0.3.0 or a deliberately documented successor.
The new specification and its scope are identified rather than resuming an already-materialized queue.
Planning and execution phase boundaries are captured separately.
Exact primary and worker model/reasoning-effort cohorts are retained and are not extrapolated into the former higher tiers.
The pre-existing dirty working tree is reconciled explicitly before Taskledger creates assignments; unrelated user changes are not attributed to the run.
New requirements, tasks, criteria, dependencies, submissions, corrections, integrations, Git diffs, and token events are measured as checkpoint deltas.

comparison_policy.primary: Evaluate workflow overhead and within-run task-family consistency for this small-scope sample.
comparison_policy.cross_project: Use financial-tracker only for model-matched workflow mechanisms such as recovery/resume frequency, context replay, compactions, approval cycles, and review corrections. Do not use raw tokens per task as a cross-project effectiveness estimate.
comparison_policy.future_value: This run establishes a small-scope v0.3.0 baseline. A later similar rust_but_verify task family can provide the clean comparison that the architecture-heavy financial-tracker history cannot.
